description: Plan C0: twin-only realism screen of the double-cart lab rig's classical controller (design/screen.py; raw runs in design/_screen/, not committed). Truth: the Lagrangian twin of lablib.setup with the realism effects, RK4 with 8 substeps per 1 ms sample. Firmware replica: 1 kHz, the design's tables, TVLQR and discrete LQR, the sensors, delay and current lag, rates from filtered differences ('diff', tau_f 2 ms, the baseline) or an EKF on the nominal twin ('ekf', q_acc (1, 10)). Scenarios: 'swingup' (hanging rest, catch at 4.0 s, to 8 s) and 'balance' (2 deg lean per link, 0.45 N 40 ms tip push at 2 s, to 7 s).

criteria.note: ok = the run finishes, |x| stays below the rail end, every link within 2 deg of upright over the last 2 s

effects.mass: link parts (tube, hubs, encoder head and board, magnet, tip cap, cable) lumped into the links; masses, lengths, COM shifts and the cart spread
effects.drive: motor constants (R, L, k_t, J_m), gear ratio, pulley radius, belt stiffness and damping
effects.fbase: carriage Coulomb + viscous friction, motor Coulomb + viscous friction (compensated in volts by 'comp')
effects.fjoint: Coulomb (tc_joint1/2) + viscous friction in both pendulum joints
effects.cable: the encoder cable: a spring and drag across joint 1, drag along the rail
effects.sensor: 14-bit joint encoders with white noise (0.03 deg rms nominal), the motor encoder through the belt
effects.loop: 2 ms whole-sample delay + the armature lag L/R (0.33 ms)
effects.ripple: commutation ripple (2 %) and cogging (0.2 N), 14 per motor revolution

verdict: Feasible with margin. The unchanged classical controller of design.json (swing-up, catch, discrete LQR) passes with every effect at its nominal value and in all 48 Monte Carlo draws over the ranges of realism.json, provided the rates come from an EKF on the nominal model (or the joint encoders are 16-bit class). With the AS5048-class 14-bit encoders, filtered differences are only marginal: the nominal rig passes (0.6 deg) but the voltage chatters at 9 V rms and peaks at the 24 V limit, and 12 of 48 Monte Carlo draws limit-cycle at 2-4 deg (all with joint noise of 0.055 deg rms or more; the tail deviation follows the noise, Spearman 0.97). The joint Coulomb friction budget is about 1e-3 N m on joint 2 and about 5e-3 N m on joint 1 (5-25x the assumed 2e-4 N m of small ball bearings), so the 0.35 m links take ordinary bearings, unlike the cart quad (5e-5 N m). The cart Coulomb compensation helps (tail 0.44 -> 0.13 deg) but is not required. Mass, drive, cable, loop delay and ripple are negligible.
recommendations: Firmware: an EKF on the nominal realistic model with process noise q_acc = (1, 10) (cart, links); (0.3, 3) to (10, 100) all pass, (10, 100) raises the balance voltage to 20 V. Keep filtered differences only as the baseline (tau_f 5-10 ms if used: 0.2 deg but 21-22 V peaks).

Joint encoders: 14-bit AS5048 class (0.03 deg rms) with the EKF; a 12-bit AS5600 or a noisy 14-bit part also passes with the EKF (0.3-0.4 deg) but fails with differences; 16 bit and up passes with either estimator.
Joint bearings: budget 1e-3 N m Coulomb on joint 2 (the limit; 2e-3 is marginal at 1.7 deg) and 5e-3 N m on joint 1. Measure them with the free-swing decay of the free model.
Cart: Coulomb compensation fc tanh(v / 2 eps) in volts with fc = the measured carriage + motor friction; 0.5 of it already gives most of the gain.

Margins at the nominal rig with the EKF: swing-up peak 15.1 V and 5.8 A, push balance 16.3 V and 8.9 A, cart within 0.39 m of the 1.0 m rail end; the Monte Carlo worst case 18.2 V, 8.5 A balance current, 0.39 m.
